text:
Both traces solve the same logic puzzle by identifying a chain of relative positions (Ash < 1713 < Vellum < 1711 < Maple) and a block of consecutive positions (Holly -> Cloth -> 1716 -> Palm), then testing possible placements. Trace 1 branches on the position of the block (Case A, B, C), while Trace 2 branches on the position of the chain (Scenario 1-5). Both explore and eliminate dead ends. Trace 1 is more linear and only re-verifies Case A once. Trace 2 gets confused about its own numbering of scenarios, leading to a second pass where it re-evaluates Set 1, Set 2, Set 3, and Set 4, resulting in multiple redundant loops.

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Case A: $x-1 = 1$. Slots 1, 2, 3, 4." end="So Case A is impossible." basis=The solver explores placing the block at slots 1-4 and systematically eliminates it by checking contradictions with Vellum and 1711 positions.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="What about Case C?" end="So Case C is impossible immediately." basis=The solver explores Case C and eliminates it due to 1716 in slot 5.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Subcase B1.2: Vellum at 6." end="So B1.2 is out." basis=The solver explores placing Vellum at slot 6 and eliminates it.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Option B2: $Pos(1713) = 5$." end="So B2 is out." basis=The solver explores placing 1713 at slot 5 and eliminates it.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Option B3: $Pos(1713) = 6$." end="So B3 is out." basis=The solver explores placing 1713 at slot 6 and eliminates it.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's quickly re-verify Case A to be sure it's impossible." end="So Case A is indeed impossible." basis=The solver re-evaluates Case A which was already eliminated earlier.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Scenario 1: $p_1=1, p_2=2, p_3=3, p_4=4, p_5=5$." end="So Scenario 1 is impossible." basis=The solver explores Scenario 1 and eliminates it.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Scenario 2: $p_1=1, p_2=2, p_3=3, p_4=4, p_5=6$." end="So Scenario 2 is impossible." basis=The solver explores Scenario 2 and eliminates it.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's check Set 3: {1, 2, 3, 5, 6}." end="So Set 3 invalid." basis=The solver explores Set 3 and eliminates it.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Set 5: {2, 3, 4, 5, 6}." end="So Set 5 invalid." basis=The solver explores Set 5 and eliminates it.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Case 1: Leather at S6." end="So Leather cannot be at S6." basis=The solver explores placing Leather at S6 and eliminates it.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's check Scenario 4: $p_1=1, p_2=2, p_3=4, p_4=5, p_5=6$." end="This is the exact same configuration as derived from Scenario 3!" basis=The solver re-evaluates the exact same set of positions that was just solved in Scenario 3.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let's check Set 4 again." end="This looks consistent." basis=The solver re-evaluates Set 4 which was already solved in Scenario 3.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Now check Set 1: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}." end="So Set 1 invalid." basis=The solver re-evaluates Set 1 which was already eliminated in Scenario 1.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Now check Set 2: {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}." end="So Set 2 invalid." basis=The solver re-evaluates Set 2 which was already eliminated in Scenario 2.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Now check Set 3: {1, 2, 3, 5, 6}." end="So Set 3 invalid." basis=The solver re-evaluates Set 3 which was already eliminated in the "Let's check Set 3" block.
